criteria.rationale: The deliverable accurately reflects all substantive workflow rules, evaluation criteria, sign-off authorities, and governance records from the request and workspace. Specifically, it applies the operative rule in record-17.txt (verified via registry.txt as revision 2, approved 2025-06-20, status in force) requiring Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams to approve price change requests, and explicitly rejects the unapproved draft record-22.txt (Purchase team alone). It also properly preserves existing sign-off authorities for TRSOs (ER, Quality, Purchase) and supplier nomination (Finance, Quality, ER, Program Managers), and clearly labels proposed change tiers, thresholds, and cycle-time targets as proposals requiring CPO confirmation rather than approved rules.

evidence.source_quote:
record-17.txt: revision 2; approved 2025-06-20; status in force; approved by process owner.
record-22.txt: revision 3; created 2025-06-23; status draft; not approved.
evidence.output_quote: Under the procedure in force (record-17, revision 2, approved 20 June 2025), every price change request needs approval from the Finance controller, the Program Manager and the Purchase team. All three are required. A later draft (record-22, revision 3) would let Purchase approve alone. It is unapproved, so this workflow does not use it.

evidence.source_quote: Price change request approvals: Finance controllers, Program managers, and Purchase teams. All three are required.
evidence.output_quote: Tier 1 changes are therefore not exempt from this rule. They can be prepared automatically, but the three approvers must still sign.

evidence.source_quote: TRSOs are reviewed and signed off by ER, Quality, and Purchase teams.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 1: TRSO sign-off by ER, Quality and Purchase.

evidence.source_quote: The final step is a formal supplier nomination, which must be documented with a full record of communication trails, negotiation summaries, internal evaluations, and signoffs from Finance, Quality, ER, and Program Managers.
evidence.output_quote: Gate 5: digital sign-off by Finance, Quality, ER and Program Manager.

evidence.source_quote: Produce the requested professional deliverables, state unresolved assumptions, and do not invent missing facts.
evidence.output_quote: The platform classifies the change into a tier using rules that Purchase, ER and Finance agree on in advance. The tiers are a proposal and need CPO confirmation.

criteria.consequence: None; governance rules and operative approval authorities are accurately preserved.
criteria.counterevidence: In the Section 4 table for Tier 1 Minor changes, the Approvals cell states 'Purchase review. Finance and Program Manager are notified. Price change approval rules still apply (see below).' While the first two sentences could momentarily suggest notification rather than approval for Finance and the Program Manager, the cell itself immediately invokes the price change approval rules in Section 5, which explicitly specifies that Tier 1 changes are not exempt from record-17 and all three approvers must still sign.

criteria.rationale: The delivered Word document fulfills all components of the user request for both executive (CPO) and technical (TechSol) audiences. It outlines the problem context for headlamp and tail lamp assemblies, defines a modular quotation structure covering base assemblies, features, design elements, and child parts/raw materials with their respective cost drivers, details the seven-step sourcing and nomination process with decision gates, specifies flexibility points and tiered handling for post-nomination design changes, defines parallel approval layers and price change governance, and provides platform requirements and open points for CPO confirmation.

evidence.source_quote: Revised sourcing and nomination workflow must involve a ‘Modular quotation structure’ to develop a plug-and-play model for cost drivers based on features, design elements, child parts and raw material used.
evidence.output_quote: Suppliers quote a cost model, not one lump-sum price. The base lamp is quoted once. Each module is priced separately and can be added, removed or re-priced without re-quoting the whole assembly.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Flexibility points: (a) rate cards and index formulas agreed at nomination let tier 1 changes be priced with no negotiation; (b) supplier quotes only the delta; (c) ER, Quality, Purchase and Finance review in parallel with a time limit, and the escalation owner is notified at the limit; (d) a roadmap of expected variants at Gate 1 lets pre-agreed option prices be held in advance; (e) each version of a module is kept, so a change can be rolled back and compared.

evidence.source_quote: Clearly define the process steps, decision gates, approval layers, and flexibility points to handle post-nomination design changes.
evidence.output_quote: Approval layers: Layer 1 is technical, with ER and Quality confirming feasibility and compliance. Layer 2 is commercial, with Purchase and Finance. Layer 3 is program, with the Program Manager confirming impact on timing and budget.

evidence.source_quote: This draft will be reviewed by the CPO and shared with the TechSol team to begin the platform development, so ensure the document is clear, logically structured, and suitable for executive and technical audiences alike.
evidence.output_quote: Core capabilities: a workflow engine with configurable gates, tiers and approval matrices, held in tables so that no code change is needed to alter them. A module and BOM-based cost model with version control. A supplier portal for quotes. Index feeds for raw materials. An immutable audit trail with digital signatures that meet Indian legal requirements.

criteria.consequence: None; the deliverable addresses all requested workflow and platform blueprint elements.

task_defect.reason: The request and workspace records are internally consistent, with registry.txt clearly establishing that record-17.txt is in force and record-22.txt is an unapproved draft.

assessment.caveat: No weighted average can offset a critical failure. Exact quotes establish traceability, not entailment. Rendering and independent human calibration remain required.
